WriteAdmission.admitted_frames.detail: A nonempty synthetic op and an already occupied pending queue satisfy the actual app admission predicate. The kernel applies the singleton encrypted-frame bound. Separate host:write-admission checks actual signed Send against SQLite, preserves rejected drafts and commits after capacity clears; this kernel fixture does not claim a signed community op.

WriteAdmission.admitted_count.detail: A nonempty op is admitted with one queued entry at the exact two-entry cap. The theorem gives the pending-count bound; a one-entry-cap control rejects the same input. This is admission through App.writeAll, not a bound on every app queue or recovery path.

WriteAdmission.admitted_bytes.detail: The real admission predicate accepts a nonempty encoded op plus existing queued bytes within a finite byte cap; the theorem applies to that result. A one-byte cap rejects. Actual Send/SQLite boundary and exhausted-budget checks, plus three mutations, run in host:write-admission.
